summary: The host side of the NAT-088 follow-up, finished. (1) kl_reader.py reads every boot of a collector archive with NAT-062's own parser, merges replay boots by offset, lists conflicts and turns lost records into exact holes; over the REAL NAT-088 archive it reads the final why=2 dump (57,665 bytes announced: head 8,192, gap 16,705, tail 32,768) with 399 of 428 records, one hole of 2,784 bytes and no conflicts, where NAT-081's replay rule had refused the boot (ladder row R9). (2) analyze_nat089.py reads launchd's boot-task lines in the kernel System Event form and the console form, the per-label spawns and exits, the heartbeat's ps -A lists, and decides the pre-registered rows A1-A8; over the real NAT-088 text it reads exactly the 3 tasks that ran and the 20 skipped, Early boot complete at kernel 193.752018 s and the heartbeat com.nat085.ps with 3 spawns (first at launchd clock 224.159344 s) alive in the last list, matching the hand reading recorded in NAT-088 (its outcome stays inconclusive). (3) The Stage A small root (19 Apple plists of the donor set minus wifid, backboardd and SpringBoard, plus the ps heartbeat) builds with tools/ios/build_pid1_chain.py --skip-job; the analyser's self-starting set is read from the plists and excludes jobs with a Disabled key (com.apple.syslogd is Disabled: true; an earlier table counted it). 60 tests; mutation pass of 535 candidates (487 killed incl. 7 ended by the timeout or the per-process memory cap, 3 survivors shown equivalent, 45 do not parse). Nothing here ran on a phone.

acceptance.1_kl_reader: test_nat089.py Reader/ReaderEdges (hand-built dumps with every number written out: records, drops, holes, conflicts, replay merge, gap marker, refused dumps, off-grid offsets) and RealArchive: the real NAT-088 archive gives 399 of 428 records, one hole (33,441-36,225), no conflicts; artifacts/nat-089/replay-nat088.json is the analysis over it.

Row outcomes other than the NAT-088 control follow from hand-built inputs only (no Stage A text exists yet).
acceptance.3_small_root: tools/ios/build_pid1_chain.py --skip-job built artifacts/nat-089/pid1-stageA/root.apfs (4,194,304 bytes, sha256 90c85ffb...); stage-a-jobs.json lists the 20 plists with sha256; read_jobs gives 7 self-starting Apple jobs (the 8th candidate, syslogd, is Disabled: true) and the heartbeat; test_the_stage_a_tree_has_seven_self_starting_apple_jobs_not_eight pins it.

findings: The first mutation pass (531 mutants) left 72 survivors: weak tests (hours in launchd_clock, duplicate dedupe, analyze()/main() untested, blank lines, refused dumps, off-grid offsets, three-boot conflicts, hole merging, default arguments, panic text) and one dead statement (`holes, _ = holes_of(m)` in text_of, removed). 18 tests were added. The second pass left 9 survivors; 6 more tests (a length-zero and a one-byte final dump, the isolated command line, the JSON indentation) killed 6 and 3 are equivalent.

The 8-worker mutation passes held 15.8 GiB of host RAM (a mutant that loops while appending ran to the 240 s timeout): the owner asked to stay under 12 GB. mutate_nat089.py now caps each test process at 1.5 GiB (RLIMIT_AS) and runs 4 workers with a 120 s timeout; the final pass is the capped one.

Reading the stock plists for the Stage A table showed that com.apple.syslogd carries `Disabled: true` (so launchd does not start it by itself), that cfprefsd.xpc.daemon.system and containermanagerd.system are disabled while a feature flag is off, and that 8 plists carry LimitLoadToSessionType (7 `System`, distnoted `System` only when a flag is on). The first draft counted 8 self-starting Apple jobs; read_jobs now excludes disabled jobs (7) and the table lists the raw `disabled` and `limit_session` of every job.

launchd's `Unable to find persona with type 6` (NAT-088) is PERSONA_SYSTEM_PROXY (bsd/sys/persona.h:45); personas_bootstrap() in the project's XNU creates no persona, so the lookup returns ESRCH until user space allocates one (source review, bsd/kern/kern_persona.c:96-125).
established: The real NAT-088 returned text, read without refusing the replay boot, shows exactly the 3 boot tasks that ran and the 20 skipped, Early boot complete at kernel 193.752018 s, 52 launchd lines, 3 ps -A lists and the heartbeat's 3 spawns, as hand-read in NAT-088.
The Stage A small root exists with the recorded hash and holds 19 Apple plists plus the heartbeat; 7 Apple jobs are self-starting by their own plists.
The tests and the mutation pass above.
not_established: That any Apple daemon runs on the S24, that the persona warning is harmless for them, that jobs with LimitLoadToSessionType load in the user/501 domain launchd used for the heartbeat, or anything about display, input, GPU or SpringBoard: no Stage A text exists.
That the analyser's rows read a real Stage A text correctly beyond the hand-built cases and the NAT-088 control; what the holes and the announced gap contained.

That the APFS container holds the plists as the tree does: a byte search of root.apfs does not find them, so the container is tied to the tree by the builder and the recorded hash only (the same builder produced NAT-084's root, which ran).
